emails.subject: Follow-up on Recent Incidents & Injury Report Procedures
emails.body:
Hi Christina, Juan, and Hannah,

I wanted to touch base with everyone about a few things related to student safety incidents we've had over the past couple weeks.

First, I noticed we had a couple of injury reports come through last week that didn't have complete follow-up documentation. Christina, I think one was from the gym class incident on Wednesday - could you send me any additional notes you have on that? I want to make sure we have everything on file in case parents follow up.

Second, Juan, I know you've been handling the bullying situation with the 7th graders that was reported before winter break. Do you have a status update on how that's progressing? I'd like to include it in my monthly safety summary for the principal.

Also, Hannah - I'm planning to schedule our quarterly safety incident review meeting for early February. I'll send out some date options by end of week. We should go through all the reports from fall and discuss any patterns we're noticing.

One more thing - I'm updating our incident response procedures and want to make sure everyone's on the same page about the new injury report form. I'll send that out separately, but wanted to give you a heads up.

Let me know if you have any questions or if there are any other safety concerns I should be aware of.

Thanks,
Erin

I've been going through the maintenance logs, and several fountains haven't been serviced since spring. With the new school year starting, I'd like to get ahead of any potential issues. I'm planning to have our vendor come through and do a full inspection and filter replacement on all units across both buildings.

Erin, could you let me know which areas would be best for scheduling this work? I'm thinking we could do the elementary wing first, then move to the secondary building. Jeffrey, I'll need your team to help with access to the mechanical areas - some of the plumbing connections are a bit tight to get to.

Also, I noticed the water cooler in the main office has been running a bit slower than usual. I'm going to have that checked out as well since we're doing the overall maintenance.

Let me know what works with your schedules. I'm hoping we can knock this out before October if possible.

Lauren

emails.body:
Hi Sarah,

I wanted to touch base regarding the situation we discussed yesterday. I've completed the initial documentation and wanted to get your input before we move forward with the next steps.

A few things I'm working through:

1. The injury report from the incident needs to be finalized - I have most of the details but want to make sure we have consistent accounts from all staff members who were present. Can you confirm the timeline you observed?

2. I'm also flagging that there may be some underlying interpersonal dynamics at play here that go beyond what happened. I want to make sure we're addressing the root cause and not just the immediate issue.

I know this is sensitive, so I want to be thorough and make sure we're handling everything appropriately. Do you have time to grab coffee tomorrow morning before school starts? I'd like to walk through the documentation together.

Erin

emails.subject: Follow-up on Water Quality Testing Schedule
emails.body:
Hi Lauren and Erin,

I wanted to touch base about the lead testing we need to get done across the district schools. We've been putting this off longer than we should, and I think we need to nail down a timeline before the end of the month.

I've been coordinating with the contractor, and they can come out starting next week to do the initial water quality assessments at the elementary schools. The drinking water fountains are priority, but we should also include the kitchen and bathroom fixtures in our scope.

Lauren - can you confirm which schools are on the schedule first? I want to make sure we're not disrupting any major events or testing periods.

Erin - I'll need your help getting access to the mechanical rooms and utility closets at each location. The testing team will need to check the main lines and take samples from several points.

Once we get the lead testing results back, we can figure out if any remediation work is needed. I'm hoping everything comes back clean, but better to know now than have this hanging over our heads.

Let me know your availability for a quick call this week to go over the details.

Thanks,
Rodney

They'll need access to the mechanical rooms and will be collecting samples from our drinking water fountains and kitchen lines. The whole process should take about 2-3 days total.

Theresa - I'll need you to notify the principals so they can let staff know about any minor disruptions. It shouldn't affect classes, but I want to be transparent about what's happening.

Lauren - once we get the results back, can you help me organize the documentation? I want to make sure everything is properly filed and easy to reference if anyone asks about our drinking water safety.

Let me know if you have any questions or concerns about the schedule. I'm hoping we can get this wrapped up early in the month so we have time to address anything if needed.

A few things I wanted to flag:

emails.body:
Hi Rodney and Norman,

I wanted to touch base about the water systems testing we discussed last week. I've been coordinating with the contractor, and they're ready to move forward with the lead testing at both the elementary and middle school buildings.

They're proposing to start the first week of next month at Lincoln Elementary. The testing will take about 2-3 days per building, and they'll need access to the main water lines and several drinking fountains throughout each facility. I'll take the lead on scheduling the actual dates once you both confirm your availability to be on-site.

A few questions before we lock anything in:

I wanted to touch base with you about the lead testing we need to get scheduled for the water systems across our buildings. As you know, we've been meaning to move forward on this for a while now.

I've been coordinating with our facilities lead, and we're looking at getting the drinking water tested at all three campuses sometime next month. The contractor quoted us about two weeks for the initial testing, so I'm thinking we should aim for early March to avoid conflicts with spring break.

A few things I wanted to run by you:

1. Do we need to notify families ahead of time about the water quality testing, or should we just document everything on our end?

2. I'll take the lead on scheduling the actual testing appointments, but I wanted to confirm which buildings should be prioritized. Should we start with the elementary school since that's where most of our younger students are?

3. Once we get the results back, who should be the lead point person for reviewing the data? I'm assuming it'll go through your office first?

Let me know your thoughts on timing and next steps. I can also send over the contractor's proposal if you need to review it before we move forward.

Thanks,
Lauren

emails.subject: Follow-up on EdTech Vendor Contracts - Need Your Input

I've been coordinating with a few EdTech vendors who've submitted proposals, and I'm trying to narrow down our options. The main contenders right now are:

1. The integrated platform we demoed last month (good features, but higher annual cost)
2. The modular vendor solution that would let us pick and choose components
3. The incumbent contract renewal (most cost-effective, but limited new functionality)

Before I schedule the full committee meeting, I wanted to get your take on the contract terms and implementation timeline for each. Do you have any availability next week to go through these together? I'm flexible on timing.

Also, if you've had a chance to talk to any of your teachers about what they'd actually want to use in the classroom, that would be really helpful. I want to make sure we're selecting a vendor that will actually get used rather than just checking a box.

Let me know what works for your schedule.

Jessica

emails.subject: EdTech Vendor Contracts - Need Your Input on Selection

Right now we're looking at three different vendors for our learning management system. Each one has a different contract structure and pricing model, which is where things get complicated from a budget standpoint. I've got the initial proposals, but the terms vary pretty significantly - one wants a 3-year commitment with an upfront payment, another is month-to-month but at a higher per-user cost, and the third has some bundled services that might actually save us money overall if we consolidate some other tools.

Before I present these to the superintendent, I wanted to walk through the financial implications with you. Do you have time next week to sit down and go over the contract details? I'm thinking we should also loop in someone from instruction to make sure we're not just looking at this from a cost perspective.

Joseph

emails.subject: Water Quality Testing Schedule - Need Your Input
emails.body:
Eduardo and Norman,

I wanted to touch base about the upcoming water quality assessments we need to coordinate across the district. As you know, we've been planning to conduct comprehensive testing on our drinking water systems, and I'd like to take the lead on scheduling the initial phase.

Our water quality consultant recommended we start with the older buildings first, particularly the elementary schools. They want to run lead testing on all the main lines and fixtures to establish a baseline. I'm thinking we should begin with the north campus since that building has the oldest infrastructure.

Eduardo, I know you've been managing the maintenance schedules - would early March work for getting crews in place? We'll need to coordinate with facilities to ensure minimal disruption during school hours. The testing itself shouldn't take more than a couple days per building.

Norman, can you help me identify which fixtures we should prioritize? I'm assuming the kitchen areas and bathrooms where students have direct access to drinking water, but let me know if there are other spots you think we should include.

I'll lead the communication with the testing company to confirm their availability and get a detailed scope. Once I hear back, I'll send over the specific requirements and any prep work we need to do beforehand.

Let me know your thoughts and availability to discuss this further.

Thanks,
Donna

Following up on what we discussed in yesterday's meeting about the federal funding we received - I wanted to touch base on a few items before we finalize the allocation plan.

I've been reviewing the guidelines from the grants we're managing, and there are some specific requirements around how we can distribute these resources across departments. The ESSER funding has some different allowable uses compared to what we received under the earlier CARES framework, and I want to make sure we're compliant across the board.

I'd like to schedule a quick call with the three of you next week to walk through the breakdown. Debbie, I'll need your input on the facilities side since we discussed some capital improvements. Joyce, I'm hoping you can weigh in on staffing considerations for the academic programs. And Brandon, we should align on the timeline for rolling out any professional development components we're planning to fund.

Also, I noticed we still have some ARP funds that haven't been allocated yet. Before we commit those, I want to make sure we're being strategic about it given the sunset dates on some of this money.

Can you all take a look at the spreadsheet I'm attaching and come back with any questions? I'm flexible on timing for the meeting - just let me know what works for your schedules.

Thanks,
Joseph

emails.subject: ESSER Fund Allocation Timeline - Need Your Input

As you know, we've been working through the ARP funds (the third tranche of CARES Act relief), and I'm trying to nail down our spending timeline for the final year. We've committed about 65% of the total allocation across the buildings, but I want to make sure we're being strategic with what's left.

I was thinking we should prioritize the literacy intervention programs and some of the tech infrastructure upgrades we discussed in the fall. I know your team had some specific needs for the elementary schools - could you send over that list again? I want to make sure we're addressing the learning loss priorities that came out of our recovery plan.

Also, do you have a sense of whether we need to encumber funds by end of Q2, or do we have flexibility into Q3? I want to give the building principals realistic timelines for their project requests.

Could we grab 30 minutes next week to go through the numbers? I'm pretty open Wednesday or Thursday afternoon.

Joseph

emails.subject: ESSER Fund Allocation Timeline - Need Your Input

I'm working through the final allocation plan for our remaining ESSER III funds and wanted to touch base with you before I present to the cabinet next week.

As you know, we've already committed a good portion of the ARP funds to learning loss initiatives and staff retention bonuses. For the remaining ESSER dollars, I'm looking at three main buckets: facility upgrades (HVAC improvements in the elementary buildings), technology infrastructure, and professional development.

I pulled together some numbers based on what other comparable districts have done with their CARES Act funding, and I think we're in a decent position. However, I want to make sure I'm not missing anything from the instructional side before we lock this in.

Could you review the attached breakdown and let me know if there are any gaps or priorities from your department that should factor in? I know facilities has been a priority, but I want to make sure we're balancing that with classroom needs.

Also, just a heads up - the state is getting stricter about documentation. Make sure any requests you have are tied to COVID-related learning loss or recovery efforts, as that's what the feds are tracking.

Let me know your thoughts when you get a chance. I'd like to finalize this by Friday if possible.

emails.subject: Updated Safety Incident Documentation Procedures
emails.body:

I wanted to touch base with everyone about some changes we're implementing for how we document and track safety-related incidents going forward. As you know, we've had a few situations this year where our reporting timelines have been inconsistent, and I'd like to streamline the process.

Starting next month, all staff members will need to submit incident documentation through the new online portal rather than emailing forms directly. This includes any reports related to student injuries, falls, or other accidents that occur on campus. The system will automatically timestamp submissions and create a backup, which should help us maintain better records.

I'm also working with our counseling team to improve how we cross-reference incident reports with any behavioral concerns. For example, if a student is involved in a physical altercation or there are bullying allegations, we want to make sure those details are captured in one centralized location so nothing falls through the cracks.

Can you each let me know by Friday if you have any concerns about transitioning to the new system? Samantha, I know your office handles a lot of the initial intake information—I'd like to schedule a quick training session with you next week if you're available.

Thanks for your continued attention to keeping our students safe.

Best,
Erin

Do you have any concerns about locking in with one vendor for that long? Also, I'd love to know if you've heard any feedback from teachers about the platforms they've tried so far.

Hope you're doing well. I'm working through our COVID Relief Fund spending plan and wanted to touch base with you before we finalize anything with the board.

As you know, we've got remaining ESSER funds from the CARES Act allocations, plus we still have a decent chunk of the ARP funds to deploy. I've been reviewing the federal compliance requirements and our current utilization rates, and I think we need to be strategic about how we allocate what's left.

I'm leaning toward dedicating more of the remaining ARP funds toward the learning loss initiatives in secondary math and literacy, but I wanted to get your perspective on the instructional side before I build out the formal proposal. Do you think that's where we'd see the most impact, or would you recommend a different approach?

Also, I need to confirm the deadline for obligating the remaining ESSER funds - I believe it's coming up faster than people realize, so we should probably schedule a quick meeting with curriculum and your team to align on priorities.

Can you find some time next week to sync up? I'm pretty flexible.

Thanks,
Joseph

emails.subject: ESSER Fund Allocation Timeline - Need Input from Department Heads

I wanted to touch base on where we stand with our remaining ARP funds before the end of the fiscal year. As you know, we've been working through the CARES Act allocations and the subsequent ESSER tranches, and I want to make sure we're on track with our spending plan.

1. Steven - Can you confirm whether the technology upgrades we discussed in March are still a priority for your department? We had allocated $120K from ESSER III for that.

2. Samantha - I know you mentioned some staffing needs for summer programming. Do you have a finalized budget for that initiative? If we're moving forward, we should get POs out this week.

3. Anthony - How are we tracking on the professional development spending? I want to make sure we're not leaving any of those funds on the table.

I'm planning to present a final reconciliation to the superintendent by June 15th, so ideally I'd like to hear back from everyone by end of day Thursday. Let me know if you have any questions or if you'd like to sync up in person.

Joseph

emails.subject: ESSER & ARP Funds - Budget Planning Meeting This Week

Hope everyone's doing well. I wanted to touch base about our remaining COVID relief allocations before we finalize the 2024-25 budget. We still have some flexibility with our ESSER III funds, and I want to make sure we're being strategic about how we use them before the deadline.

As you know, the CARES Act funding wrapped up a while back, but we've got until September 2024 to obligate our ARP funds. I've been reviewing the carryover amounts and wanted to get your input on priorities:

- Kevin, can you send over the updated tech infrastructure needs from your department? We had discussed using some of these funds for the laptop refresh.
- Jennifer, I'll need your final numbers on the tutoring/intervention programs you wanted to expand. That seems like a solid use of remaining ARP money.
- William, I know facilities has been waiting on some equipment - let me know what's realistic to get ordered and installed by the deadline.

1. From your end-user perspective, which vendor seemed most intuitive for teachers to use? I want to make sure we're not just picking based on cost.

2. Did you notice any significant differences in their implementation timelines? We're hoping to get everything rolled out by August, and I want to make sure the vendor we select can actually meet that deadline.

3. Have you had a chance to look at the professional development offerings each vendor includes? That's going to be important for adoption.

I'm planning to present the top two options to the tech committee next Thursday, so if you could get me your notes by Wednesday morning, that would be really helpful.

Let me know if you want to grab coffee and talk through this in person—sometimes it's easier than email.

We still have a decent chunk of our ARP funds available, and I'm trying to map out the best use cases. I know you've mentioned some technology and infrastructure needs in your area. The deadline for obligating these dollars is coming up faster than I'd like, so I'd rather get ahead of it.

A few quick questions:
- Are there any CARES Act carryover items from the earlier rounds that we should prioritize?

As you know, we're looking at restructuring how we deliver services across the elementary schools, particularly around our resource room model and co-teaching placements. I'm also thinking we should review our current IEP meeting procedures to ensure they're streamlined but still thorough.

Mark – can you pull together some data on current caseloads and how students are distributed across our buildings? I'd like to see where we have the most need.

Let's plan to meet next Thursday at 2 PM to go over what you've gathered. We can use that to shape our next steps and timeline. If that doesn't work, let me know and we'll find another time.

Thanks for your help on this. I know our special education team is stretched thin, and I want to make sure any changes we make actually improve things for our students and staff.

emails.body:
Hi Brian,

I wanted to touch base with you about some of the changes coming down from central office regarding our special education program. I got the memo last week but wanted to discuss before our next department meeting.

From what I understand, they're looking at restructuring how we handle IEP meetings next year—something about consolidating some of our pull-out services and integrating more co-teaching models in the general ed classrooms. I think there's some merit to it, but I'm also concerned about how this affects our caseloads and whether we'll have adequate support staff.

Also, I heard there might be changes to how we're documenting progress on IEPs, but I haven't seen the specifics yet. Do you know if you've received more details on that side of things?

I'd really like to get your perspective since you work closely with the elementary SPED team. Are you hearing anything from your contacts down there? I'm trying to get a sense of whether this is district-wide or just impacting our building.

Let me know if you have time to grab coffee this week and talk through this. I want to make sure we're on the same page before we have to roll this out to the teachers.

Thanks,
Lori

emails.body:
Scott, Jeffrey, Diana,

I wanted to touch base regarding the federal funds we've been working through. As you know, we've received allocations from multiple rounds of support, and I'm trying to get a clearer picture of how we're tracking everything across departments.

Specifically, I'm looking at our accounting for the various tranches we received and want to make sure we're aligned on how we're categorizing and spending. I know we discussed some of this during our budget meetings, but I need to nail down a few specifics:

1. Can each of you send me an updated breakdown of how your departments plan to use the funds allocated to you? I want to make sure we're staying within the guidelines and timelines we're working with.

2. I'm also pulling together documentation for our compliance file, so I'll need copies of any proposals or justifications you submitted when we were dividing up that money.

I'm also going to need to schedule time with our grant compliance officer to review everything before we move forward with any major purchases or commitments. We want to make sure we're doing this correctly given all the requirements attached to this support.

Can we set up a call early next week to go over the details? I'm flexible on timing.

Ebony - could you help me identify which buildings are priorities? I want to make sure we're testing the older wings first, especially the elementary building.

Norman - when you get a chance, can you send me the maintenance log for the water lines in the north corridor? I want to include that info when I talk to the testing company.

Let me know what days work best for you both. We should probably plan for at least 2-3 days depending on how many fixtures they need to sample for water quality.

Thanks,

emails.subject: Professional Development Opportunity - Facilities Management Training
emails.body:
Hello Kathy, Angela, and Randall,

I wanted to reach out to let you know about an upcoming professional development opportunity that may be of interest to our maintenance team.

The district is offering a half-day workshop on "Best Practices in Building Systems and Energy Efficiency" scheduled for Thursday, March 14th from 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM in the Central Office Training Room. This session will cover:

• HVAC system maintenance and troubleshooting
• Energy-efficient facility practices
• Safety protocols and equipment updates
• Q&A with district facilities director

Attendance is voluntary but highly encouraged. If you're interested in participating, please let me know by March 7th so I can register you with HR. Light refreshments will be provided.

Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions or would like more information about the training.

Best regards,
Lauren Herrera
Maintenance Staff

emails.subject: Classroom Supply Order - Please Submit Requests by Friday
emails.body:
Hi Christina, Robert, and Kylie,

I wanted to send a quick reminder that we need to submit our classroom supply orders for next month by this Friday, October 13th. Please review the attached supply list and let me know if there are any items you'd like to add or adjust.

Some items that are running low:
- Dry erase markers
- Printer paper
- Tissues and hand sanitizer
- Pencils and erasers

If you have specific requests beyond the standard order, please send them to me by end of day Thursday so I can include them in the submission to the main office.

Also, just a heads up that we'll be reorganizing the supply closet next Tuesday during planning period if anyone wants to help.

Thanks,
Erin Macias

emails.subject: Upcoming Field Trip - Permission Forms Due by Friday
emails.body:
Dear Samuel and Kevin,

I hope this email finds you well. I wanted to reach out regarding the upcoming field trip scheduled for next month.

Trip Details:
- Date: Tuesday, April 16th
- Destination: Science Museum and Planetarium
- Grade Levels: 8th and 9th grade
- Departure: 8:00 AM from school
- Return: 2:30 PM

Parent permission forms have been distributed to all students and are also available on the school website. Please remind your students that completed forms must be submitted by Friday, April 5th. Students without signed permission forms will not be able to attend.

The cost is $12 per student, which covers admission and transportation. Payment can be made online through the school portal or in cash to the main office.

If you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out. We're looking forward to a great educational experience for our students.

Best regards,
Debra Wang
School Counselor

emails.subject: Parking Lot Reminders for Staff
emails.body:
Hi Michele and Lauren,

I wanted to send out a quick reminder about parking lot procedures as we head into the busy season.

Please keep the following in mind:

• Use designated staff parking areas only
• Arrive early enough to find parking before the morning bell
• Do not park in visitor or student spaces
• Keep fire lanes and loading zones clear at all times
• Report any parking violations or safety concerns to the main office

Thank you for your cooperation in keeping our parking areas organized and safe for everyone.

Best regards,
Robert Silva

cpra_requests.title: Lead Testing in Water Systems
cpra_requests.description: Request for communications about lead testing in school water systems
cpra_requests.request_text: Please provide all emails, memos, and communications regarding lead testing, water quality testing, or drinking water safety in school facilities from January 1, 2023 to present. This includes communications about test results, remediation efforts, and communications with parents or regulatory agencies.

cpra_requests.title: COVID Relief Fund Allocation
cpra_requests.description: Request for communications about federal COVID relief fund allocation
cpra_requests.request_text: All communications, including emails and attachments, related to the allocation, distribution, or use of federal COVID-19 relief funds (ESSER, CARES Act, ARP) received by the district. Include discussions of spending priorities, vendor selections, and board presentations from March 2020 to present.

cpra_requests.title: Special Education Program Changes
cpra_requests.description: Request for communications about special education program modifications
cpra_requests.request_text: Please provide all emails and documents discussing changes, modifications, or updates to special education programs, IEP processes, or special education staffing from August 2023 to present. Include communications with parents, staff discussions, and policy updates.

cpra_requests.title: EdTech Vendor Contracts
cpra_requests.description: Request for communications about educational technology vendor selection
cpra_requests.request_text: All emails and communications regarding the selection, evaluation, or contracting with educational technology vendors, including but not limited to learning management systems, student information systems, and digital curriculum platforms from January 2024 to present.

cpra_requests.title: Student Safety Incidents
cpra_requests.description: Request for communications about student safety incidents and responses
cpra_requests.request_text: Please provide all emails and reports regarding student safety incidents, including but not limited to bullying reports, playground injuries requiring medical attention, and security concerns from the current school year (August 2024 to present). Exclude routine minor incidents.
